travelAdvisory.summary:
Exercise normal precautionin Singapore.
Singapore is generally a safe destination for travelers.
Review our travel guidance for Singapore to learn how to prepare for a safe trip.

healthcare.summary: Health & medication guide for Singapore. Emergency numbers (995/999), pharmacy tips, restricted medications (strict drug laws), travel insurance, water safety, and vaccination recommendations.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers from most countries. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Singapore is dengue-endemic — take mosquito precautions (use repellent, wear long sleeves at dusk).

pharmacy.hours: Most pharmacies open 10am-10pm daily. Guardian, Watsons, and Unity (government-run) pharmacy chains are widely available. Some 24-hour pharmacies exist. Hospital pharmacies are also available for specific needs.
pharmacy.tips: Many common OTC medications are available. Singapore has strict pharmaceutical regulations — some medications available OTC elsewhere require prescriptions here. Generic medications are available. Hospital pharmacies serve specific patient needs. Chemist shops are easy to find in malls.

water.notes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Singapore. Tap water is treated and meets WHO standards. Bottled water is also widely available.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Singapore has excellent food safety standards. Hawker centers (outdoor food courts) are held to strict hygiene standards — the government regularly inspects them. Singapore's hawker food is generally very safe. Water and ice in drinks are safe at licensed establishments.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not required but strongly recommended. Singapore is extremely expensive for healthcare.
travelInsurance.tips: Singapore is one of the world's most expensive cities for healthcare. A hospital stay can cost 500-2,000+ SGD per day. A specialist consultation costs 100-250 SGD. Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is strongly recommended — serious emergencies may require evacuation to another country.

healthcare.qualityNotes: Singapore has one of the best healthcare systems in the world. Both public and private hospitals are excellent with internationally trained doctors and universally English-speaking staff. Singapore is a major medical tourism hub. Healthcare is expensive — among the highest in Asia — but quality is exceptional.

medications.prescriptionRules: Singapore has strict prescription requirements. Medications prescribed by foreign doctors are NOT automatically accepted — a Singapore doctor may need to re-prescribe. Controlled substances require Singaporean authorization. Some common medications (like certain antihistamines) are available OTC.

restrictedMeds.name: Diazepam (Valium) and benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Requires Singaporean prescription or authorization from the Health Sciences Authority (HSA). Bring your foreign prescription and doctor's letter. Singapore customs is very strict about controlled substances.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Small quantities for personal use may be allowed with documentation, but a Singaporean prescription is safer.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription or HSA authorization. Singapore takes a zero-tolerance approach to drug trafficking.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Requires Singaporean prescription or special authorization from HSA. Contact the Singaporean embassy before traveling with ADHD medications. Penalties for unauthorized possession are severe.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Singapore — severe penalties including death for trafficking. There are no exceptions. Do not bring any cannabis products, including CBD.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For any potentially controlled medications, carry the original prescription and HSA authorization if required. Declare all medications at customs.

connectivity.simOptions: Singtel, StarHub, or M1 tourist SIMs at Changi vending machines. SGD 15-38.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Excellent free WiFi everywhere. Wireless@SG is government network.
connectivity.bestOption: Singtel tourist SIM at Changi. World-class 5G coverage.

cultural.tipping: Not expected. 10% service charge + 7% GST usually added. Don't tip at hawker centres.
cultural.dressCode: Casual. Smart casual for nice restaurants. Bring jacket for AC.
cultural.greetings: Handshake. English is common language. 'Hello' works universally.
cultural.haggling: Only at some tourist markets. Singapore is a fixed-price society.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free. Among easiest countries to visit.

hospitals.name: Singapore General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Singapore's largest public hospital. Excellent facilities, English-speaking staff throughout.

hospitals.name: Mount Elizabeth Hospital
hospitals.notes: Premier private hospital. International patient services, accepts major international insurance.

immediate: Monitor NEA PSI (Pollution Standards Index) readings hourly during haze periods
PSI 101-200 (Unhealthy): minimize outdoor activity, wear N95 mask outdoors
PSI 201-300 (Very Unhealthy): stay indoors, all outdoor exercise should stop
PSI >300 (Hazardous): avoid all outdoor exposure, seal windows and doors
after: PSI readings available on myENV app
Haze typically improves with wind direction changes — monitor NEA forecasts

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 999)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (999) and ambulance (995) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the LEFT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is required for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
